_comment: Each entry is one listing page to scrape. `list_selector` matches one card/row per scholarship. The rest are CSS selectors RELATIVE to that card. Run `python scripts/inspect_page.py <url>` (needs real internet access) to print candidate selectors, then confirm with your browser's 'Inspect Element'. Sites change their HTML often -- if a source stops returning results, this is almost always the first place to fix.
keywords_comment: A scraped scholarship is kept only if its title+description contains at least one of these (case-insensitive). This filter runs on EVERY source, so even a general/all-majors listing page only contributes relevant rows. Edit freely.

notes: enabled:false sources are skipped -- flip to true once you've verified selectors AND checked the site's robots.txt/ToS.
Add as many source objects as you want; the scraper loops over all of them and applies the `keywords` filter to each.
If a site renders listings via JavaScript (nothing shows up in `curl` or `requests`), plain requests+BeautifulSoup won't see them -- see the Playwright note in scripts/scrape_scholarships.py.

Good candidates to add next: your university's CS/Stats department scholarship page, ACM, IEEE Computer Society, the American Statistical Association (amstat.org) awards page -- these are narrower, less likely to block bots, and squarely on-topic.
